result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Scanned 54 nongenerated production, configuration, infrastructure, and script files for credentials & secrets patterns; excluded tests, generated migrations and compiled infrastructure, third-party generated frontend assets, prior assessments, skills, and .github/agents.

Mapping review: infra/main.bicep:59 constructs a deployment-specific SQL administrator password using a fixed format and deterministic uniqueString of resourceGroup().id, which includes public subscription/resource-group metadata. Lines 67-68 install the resulting password. No literal complete password or cryptographic key is embedded; determinism and public inputs establish a predictable-password issue (CWE-330, outside these five rules), not by themselves a confirmed hard-coded-password/credential instance under CWE-259 or CWE-798. All derivation constants and credential values are omitted.

Permission review: infra/main.bicep:79-84 and azure-setup.sh:111-116 admit Azure-wide SQL network connections, but do not themselves authorize unintended actors to read or modify SQL data. Storage containers are private and role grants target the explicitly configured application managed identity. No confirmed CWE-732 data-access permission assignment to unintended actors was established.

Logging mapping review: azure-setup.sh:200 prints a runtime-generated SQL administrator credential. That disclosure is CWE-532 (outside the requested rules), not CWE-778. The CWE-778 finding instead concerns unrecorded admin-login failures.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: LoginModel.OnPostAsync compares the submitted username and password at lines 52-54, then returns the login page for invalid credentials at lines 55-57 without recording an authentication-failure event. LoginModel has no ILogger or other audit-event mechanism (lines 18-23); neither the rejected username nor the failure outcome is logged. Consequently repeated invalid admin-login attempts cannot be identified from application authentication audit events. PhotoAlbum/appsettings.json:16-20 sets Microsoft.AspNetCore logging to Warning; ordinary framework request diagnostics do not provide a credential-validation failure event for this custom handler. Credential values are omitted.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
